utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Prosecution wanted to raise a preliminary matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. The first one relates to P431. On the 19th of November, the Chamber brought to our attention that the English and B/C/S pages uploaded in e-court did not match. We've corrected that error and have uploaded a corrected version of the exhibit. It is 65 ter 02353B, and I would ask that the Chamber authorise the replacement of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Groome, is the original or the English replaced?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Both, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both. May I take it that there's no objection against replacing both the original version and the translation of P431 to be replaced by the newly uploaded one?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you may replace both versions of P431 in e-court by the new ones uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the second issue relates to P2602. In that case, we've discovered that the English translation of that document is incorrect. We have uploaded a corrected version under document ID 021164161, and we would ask that that authorisation be given to replace the English translation of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you may replace the old English translation of P2602 by the new one uploaded as doc ID 0211-6416-1. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, before we continue, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. Weber will now continue his examination-in-chief. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On Tuesday we generally discussed some of the principles and functions of command and control. I will return to them throughout the course of your examination when we discuss some particular materials. Today, I would like to return to where we left off. We were talking about the notion of All People's Defence in the former Yugoslavia. On page 17 of Part 1, you discuss Article 97 the 1982 ONO law regarding the authority of the SFRY Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This can be found in e-court in B/C/S on page 53. Under exhibit number P3029, marked for identification. Thank you, Ms. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did the SFRY Presidency take any steps to limit the authority of the republics over their respective Territorial Defence units or Territorial Defences prior to 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and this is happening in the latter half of the 1980s under the so-called Jedinstvo plan which reviews, as I would call it, the strategic concept for the use of the SFRY armed forces transforms the General Staff of the JNA into the General Staff of the SFRY armed forces. And also then in 1990, there is the order by General Adzic, chief of the General Staff of the SFRY armed forces, to safe-guard the weapons of the TO in JNA warehouses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did this limit the authority of the republics over their respective Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I will just summarise what is described in the report. In the sense that the republics were responsible for the training, organisation, and combat readiness of the TOs, and after the -- the death President Tito in 1980, there were fears amongst some in the former Yugoslavia that some republics, in particular Slovenia and Croatia, would try to develop their TO into republican armed forces. And as is described in the report, then steps are undertaken, the ones I mentioned, in order to increase the authority of the JNA over the TO, for example, by renaming the chief of General Staff, as I indicated, and also what I didn't mention yet, the replacement of the armies as -- as -- as a geographic military structure as well as a command structure by military districts whereby, for example, the military district would cover the territory of eastern Croatia, the largest part of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as the largest part of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did the Bosnian Serb political leadership apply or adapt any of the ONO principles during the mobilisation of Bosnian Serbs into Territorial Defence units prior to May 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question, but I think it's important to clarify that when the Bosnian Serbs established their own political structures, starting in the latter half of 1991, and further expanding into the first half of 1992, obviously they also need some kind of an armed force, so steps are made to mobilise a Bosnian Serb TO. But this is a self-declared or a self-established structure which should not be confounded with the TO of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as it existed under the concept of All People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit D78, page 2 of both versions, for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, before you is going to appear the Variant A and B instructions from 19th December of 1991. I'm going to start with the first paragraph at the top of the page. The section indicates that these instructions elaborate the unified tasks, measures, and other activities that will be undertaken within the national community of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina with the aim of implementing the plebiscite decision of the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina to live in a single state. Could you please assist us first with what plebiscite decision is this a reference to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in -- I believe on 9 and 10 of November, the Bosnian Serbs organised a -- yeah, plebiscite in Bosnia-Herzegovina where the voters can express themselves or could express themselves about whether they wanted to stay in Bosnia-Herzegovina or not. I remember - and I'm not sure whether I included these documents in this report but when I worked on other cases - that, for example, the JNA facilitated the participation of its personnel in that plebiscite. I mean, JNA units deployed in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like you to also just take a look at paragraph 2 indicating "the tasks, measures, and other activities defined in these instructions will be undertaken in order to increase mobility and readiness for the defence of the interests of the Serbian people." From these two initial paragraphs, do you have any comments on what the purpose of these instructions are?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the purpose of these instructions is, I think the text is quite clear, is to -- to organise the Bosnian Serbs in order to -- to -- to be ready if needed to use military means; i.e., it means to mobilise, as is further explained in the text, police forces as well as TO. But, again, at that stage, there was a republican police in Bosnia-Herzegovina and a republican TO but no ethnically based structures. I mean, there was no Bosniak or Muslim TO or no Bosnian Croatian TO or no Bosnian Serb TO, and the same applies to the police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please have page 5 of the B/C/S original and page 4 of the English. And in the English, if we could please direct ourselves towards the bottom half of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to item 2 under the second stage of Variant A --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would note, for the record, that the same language appears under the second stage of Variant B.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- these instructions envision the mobilisation of all police forces from among the Serbian people and their gradual resubordination to JNA command. In considering the principles of All People's Defence, when would such an instruction be given?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, unless it would concern an exercise, such a decision would be taken if one of the three states would be declared; i.e., the state of war, the state of imminent threat of war, or the state of emergency.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Would a mobilisation only occur during any of those particular states?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Unless it would be for -- it would be an exercise, i.e., for training purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under item 3, it states that: "Through the responsible organs, ensure the implementation of the order on the mobilisation of reserve JNA forces and Territorial Defence units." Under this, when would such a mobilisation be undertaken according to the All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours -- I'm sorry. In my understanding under the same conditions as I have indicated in my answer to the previous question; i.e., one of the three states or for training purposes during an exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 22 of Part 2 of your report, which is P3029, e-court page 236 in the B/C/S, you note the conclusions from the Second Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina on 21 November 1991 and its decision to mobilise "Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see the document on the e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. It's in the English page 238, B/C/S page 236 of P3029. Your Honour, I see that it might be continuing on from the previous page 2, at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Theunens, in relation to these earlier conclusions, is whether the December 1991 variants are consistent with the intention to further mobilise individuals of Bosnian Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are, Your Honours, and I -- I try to include what I consider main political decisions on the Bosnian Serb level in order to provide the context for military develops [sic] we are seeing as is also expressed through the documents on the two variants.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 15 of Part 2 of your report, which can be found on the document before us in English, page 231, and B/C/S page 229, on this page, you state that: "Serb dominated 2nd Military District units also actively (and overtly) support the SDS in taking over of power in certain strategically located municipalities in BiH." How was this done?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, in -- in this conclusion, I am referring to what is discussed in detail under title 3 of section 4 of the report, i.e., implementation of Bosnian Serb strategic goals; and more specifically, the take-overs of municipalities in northern BiH between April and May 1992, which is discussed on pages 117 to 162 of Part 2 of the report, whereby we see that armed formations consisting of, I mean, generically, Bosnian Serb TO, Bosnian Serb police, sometimes volunteers/paramilitaries originating from Serbia, including units that enjoy particular relations with the minister of the interior of the Republic of Serbia, together with the JNA or, in some cases, the JNA does not participate, i.e., actually facilitates the take-over by just not intervening. So these armed formations, they take control of a number of municipalities, and when we look at these municipalities and we look at the map, well, this actually corresponds with the implementation of strategic goal number 2, namely, establishing a corridor between Krajina and Semberija.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were these take-overs implemented in a manner consistent with the Variant A and B instructions?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were. Because we see that local Serb TO and police units are being established. The SDS plays a role in that. These units are mobilised. And as I mentioned then depending on the situation, I mean, you have to look at the details of each take-over, the JNA participates or does not participate but then does not prevent a take-over. And when the JNA participates they -- there are examples that they have command and control over the take-over. But in any event, a unified and single command and control over what I would call Serb forces conducting these take-overs is established.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 2887, page 11 of the English and page 16 of the B/C/S. The Prosecution notes that only a small excerpt of this report was admitted as P97. However, this report is referenced on -- on numerous occasions in Mr. Theunens's report, in different parts of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in your report, in Part 2, in a number of footnotes but, in particular, in footnotes 810 and 32, you discuss this 20 March 1992 2nd Military District report on the elevation of the situation in its zone of responsibility. What is the context of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just asking for a general explanation of Mr. Theunens' -- why he thought this document was relevant to his review, but I might be going to this particular page in a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the context is the situation as it is say during spring 1992 in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which is marked by a degree of confusion and uncertainty about the future. Because on one hand there is the JNA. On the other hand, we see that the -- the main ethnic groups are establishing armed structures. And at that stage the future of Bosnia-Herzegovina, whether or not it will stay in Yugoslavia, has not been decided but is the subject of negotiations at the highest level even if obviously the parties are ready -- are already taking or making their preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And with respect to this 20 March 1992 report from the 2nd Military District, what information was relevant to your analysis in the context of what was going on?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shows that the 2nd Military District is providing support to the Bosnian Serbs, for example, by distributing weapons. It also shows that there is a -- I would say a coherence between the goals of the 2nd Military District as well as the SDS even if -- I think in one of the paragraphs there is some criticism on what the SDS, SDS is being too aggressive. But in conclusion, the document show there is a consistency between the goals pursued by the Bosnian Serb as established by the SDS and the 2nd Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 14 of Part 2 of your report, if we could stay on this document on e-court, but it is on -- in terms of the reference to Mr. Theunens's report, that's in e-court on English page 230 and B/C/S page 228. You note that this 2nd Military District report indicates there were 69.198 Serb volunteers in the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Military District. Does the list before you represent the breakdown of volunteers in each municipality who had been mobilised into the Territorial Defence of the SRBiH by that time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the top of the page. Because, I mean, the Bosnian Serb, if I know it, that's -- I mean, I don't see the top but I agree with your suggestion. It is indeed a detailed breakdown. I think of notice also and that -- I put that in page 14 is that when the report is discussing Bosnian Serbs, these are qualified as volunteers where when it consists the other parties, i.e., the -- the Croats or the Muslims, then it -- the -- the term paramilitary formations is used, which also shows the position the 2nd Military District of the JNA had in relation or -- or on these groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders the complete report, 65 ter 2887.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2887 receives number P3030, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 09189. Page 2 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the document coming up is in Part 2, footnote 48, of your report. Appearing before us is -- is going to be the report approved by Blagoje Adzic, forwarded to the JNA 2nd Military District on 3 April 1992. I'd like to focus your attention under task 1 in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't think we have the actual proper footnote. It's not Part 2, footnote 48.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Footnote 48 reads: "ERN B/C/S," and then a long number, "order from the SSNO Colonel -- General Adzic," dated the 3rd of April. And this seems to be a report rather than an order, Mr. Weber. Or is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe if we could see the previous page, this is the continuation of that document, possibly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you allow me, it is indeed the document I refer to and it -- I mean, the correct description is, of course, "report" instead of "order," so the text in footnote 48 may have to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, does this resolve your problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, the ERN matches but the signature does not so I'm still confused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know, if you look at the cover page, the Major-General Simonovic, he forwards the document, which consists of report of a meeting General Blagoje Adzic had, and during that meeting he also gives instructions. And actually when you look at the cover page and this is where, I mean, "confusion" between brackets, may come from, it clearly states: "Please have in mind the tasks are exclusively for your personal use." I mean "tasks" in a military context means "order," but I agree with you that the correct description of the document should have been "report."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please go to page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for those clarifications, Mr. Theunens. Again, if I could direct your attention to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone for the sake of interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Understood. I was just looking over the document. My apologies to the booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under task 1 in the middle of the page: "The command of the 2nd Military District appears to be instructed in the shortest possible term to start to form headquarters, detachments, and brigades of volunteer units and to appoint them adequate commanding staff from the JNA and to fill them with arms and equipment." It appears that the term set for this was 15 April 1992. Could you please explain to us how this task would facilitate the command and control of the 2nd Military District over the existing Bosnian Serb TO units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is as the document states, that is, that these units - I mean, headquarters, detachments and related units - have to be led by a commanding officer of the JNA, which obviously facilitates a single and unified command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 9189 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 09189 receives number P3031, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P3027.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this document is in Part 2 section 1 of your report. I see in footnotes 125 and 126, just for your assistance. These are the decisions distributed on 16 April 1992 by SRBiH Minister Of Defence Bogdan Subotic. In your report, you note these were sent to the governments of the self-declared Serb Autonomous Regions in Bosnia. What are the significance of these decisions to your analysis?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, as I explained, these -- these decisions show that the Bosnian Serbs in their -- in their - how would I say it? - in the way to creating their own state in -- in Bosnia-Herzegovina, explicitly foresee that they may have to use military means -- or they would have to use military means in order to achieve that goal. And this document then demonstrates how self-declared TO units are being mobilised following the decision on the day before of an imminent state of war by these Bosnian Serb authorities. Or by the self-declared Bosnian Serb authorities. And again, I think there is reference is made in the document on the requirement for close co-operation with the -- with the -- with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the second page of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you is the statement of reasons on this page. If we could -- we have it. The first statement states: "The municipal TO Staffs that have operated regularly so far shall remain in the same formation and establishment. Set up TO Staffs in newly formed Serbian municipalities on the same principle." Could you please tell us what the -- was the reason that there were newly formed Serbian municipalities that required the setting up of new TO Staffs by mid-April 1992.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, in -- in Bosnia-Herzegovina, as it existed at the time, i.e., one of the six republics of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, there were no Serb municipalities nor there were Bosnian Croatian or Muslim municipalities. They were all municipalities of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We see on the political level that the Bosnian Serbs are establishing their own structures, both at the, I mean, we seen the SARs, so the Serb Autonomous Regions and the Serb Autonomous Districts - SAR and SAOs - similar measures are taken on the municipal level, and obviously as I have mentioned there is a requirement also to have military structures, so they rely for that on existing TOs whereby on the basis of those they create their own structures and this is, of course, easier in municipalities with a Bosnian Serb majority, and they do the same for the police. And while doing so, they seek co-operation with the JNA as is illustrated, for example, in this document by subordinating these units to the JNA. So there they try to apply to the legislative framework as it existed in the SFRY and also under the concept of All People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Since this document is on our screen, I just want to direct your attention to the end of the statement of reasons where it states: "In preparing the instruction as well as the engagement of TO unit, achieve co-operation with JNA units, and where possible, put them under a single command." Is this statement consistent with the views you've already expressed on this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, Your Honours. And the -- where possible I explained that earlier it is at that stage the JNA is still -- I mean, the 2nd Military District, there are still a substantial number of non-Serbs part of it. And even among Serb officers in the 2nd Military District, they do not necessarily share the objective of the SDS. So that's why the -- the notion of "where possible" is included because the point of view of 2nd Military District is not entirely clear at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 43 of Part 2 of your report, in e-court English page 259, B/C/S page 257. Again, this is Exhibit P3029 marked for identification. You conclude: "The establishment of the VRS signifies that the SRBiH TO ceases to exist and that the TO SRBiH staffs and units are integrated into the VRS." Could you, at this time, just please explain to us how this happened?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. During the 16th Assembly Session on 12th of May, 1992, the creation of the VRS is announced. We see in the 1993 analysis of combat readiness report that the Main Staff of the VRS is established between 3rd of May and I believe 16 or 19 May 1992. And then orders are issued, for example there is an order by General Mladic in June, determining not only the structure of the VRS, because this has also already been ordered also by Mr. Karadzic, but also explicitly mentioning the integration of the TO and other armed structures into the VRS. And obviously this process takes some time. And I have explained in my report that, for example -- I mean, there are two examples: The Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and I believe the Herzegovina Corps where the integration of the Bosnian Serb TO into the VRS takes more time than in other areas. But then there is a September 1992 document by General Mladic which kind of creates an overview of the status of the VRS at that stage, and that document explicitly mentions that everywhere the Bosnian Serb TO has been integrated into the VRS, and this is further then also explained in the 1993 analysis of the combat readiness of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 792.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this document is in Part 2, footnote 67 and 68, of your report. Before you is a 2nd Military District order dated 11 May 1992 from Ratko Mladic. Can you please comment what General Mladic orders under item 1?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, it's explained in the text he orders to immediately mobilise and establish all war-time units in your -- and this refers to the subordinate units of the 2nd Military District. And those are to include what he describes as Serbian people, Territorial Defence, i.e., Bosnian Serb TO, as well as volunteer units. Again, these are Bosnian Serb or volunteers from Serbia. And they have to be included in -- in -- in JNA establishment units. And he also instructs to ensure command and control over these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic. Mr. Mladic, no loud speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the comment of my client was directed to the document which does not indicate anywhere the volunteer units from Serbia as the witness has mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we -- although that could have been left to cross-examination, perhaps, under the present circumstances, Mr. Theunens, could you point us as where volunteer units from Serbia are mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is correct that this specific document does not mention volunteer units from Serbia. But I was looking or I was commenting on the document in the context of the overall situation as it is existing by that date, i.e., 11 of May, 1992, in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when you were commenting, did you want to refer to Serb volunteer units or volunteer units from Serbia? Which is not exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I wanted to refer to, that -- I mean, there are different types of volunteer units or units that are called volunteer units present at that time in Bosnia-Herzegovina. As we see during the take-overs, we see that there are groups that consist -- that come from Serbia, consisting of volunteers from Serbia. Among these groups, when I refer then to groups that are active in Sarajevo, and groups I mean by that affiliated with the Radical Party, my understanding is that they consist both of volunteers, Serbian volunteers from Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as Serbs from Serbia, from outside Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the -- the proper way of telling us this would have been Serbian volunteer units not excluding those coming from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic is seeking a timeout again. Mr. Mladic, only if you lower the volume of your voice such that it is not audible for anyone else in this courtroom. Otherwise, I'll not allow any further consultations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, your voice is ... I noticed that, at the end, you were speaking at an audible volume. Any those matters could be dealt with in cross-examination and could be discussed during the breaks. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, your previous answer on page 17 was interrupted. You were stating with respect to the first part, under item 1 of this order: "Again, these are Bosnian Serb volunteers from Serbia and they have to be included in the JNA establish establishment units and he also instructs to ensure command and control over these" -- If you could please just complete your answer or if you have any other comments?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I just -- maybe there is a slip of the tongue, but I don't think I said Bosnian Serb volunteers from Serbia. These are Serb volunteer units. And I think, Your Honours, you gave a good summary. So Serb volunteer units not excluding also Serbs from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 792 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 792 receives number P3032, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1966, page 4 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you cite this document multiple times in Part 2. They are footnotes 37, 172, 262, 751, 752, and 1176. Mr. Theunens, this is General Mladic's September 1992 report on the results achieved on the front in the state of the VRS. Is this the September 1992 report that you were just earlier referring to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the second paragraph on this page and the part where General Mladic states: "The regular army consists of all units of the former Territorial Defence inherited from the earlier system of ONO ... or which were formed (self-organised) at the time the Serbian people were self-organising for the defence against the advancing Nazi-Fascism in BH in 1991." Does this statement confirm that the former SRBiH TO units were incorporated into the existing military units of the JNA once the VRS was formed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There is mention of the ONO in General Mladic's statements. Could you please comment on whether or not General Mladic's statements indicate whether the VRS was still using the territorial system based on the notion of All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. As the document states and also the -- the June order and report, I mean by report I mean the document where General Mladic explains that all TO units or Bosnian Serb TO units have been integrated, except that in the area of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, and if I'm not wrong the Herzegovina Corps and/or the Eastern Bosnia Corps. This integration goes more slowly because of local factors. But he clearly states that All People's Defence is something from the past and that the VRS is the only authorised armed force, I mean military armed force, in the SRBiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the next sentence, General Mladic states: "The decision to establish the Army of Republika Srpska ensured single command over the armed struggle from tactical to operative formations and the army as a whole." Do you have any comments on this based on the principles of command principles -- excuse me, and functions of command and control?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is fully consistent with the principles as set in SFRY armed forces doctrine, and these principles were also confirmed in the SRBH Law on Army I mean, the three principles of command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, I will return to the topic of the SFRY forces and the ONO after we discuss some additional evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm about to move into a brand new topic. If this is a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will take the break after Mr. Theunens has been escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens -- Mr. Weber, I noticed that speed of speech is still problematic. We take a break and we resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to come in, I'd like to put on the record that the revised English translation for P3008 has been uploaded into e-court. It was about the word "supervise" against "control." I do understand that the translation which says "supervise" has been corrected to "control." It is transcript pages 20119 and 120, and transcript page 20214 and 215. Since the translation issue was the only reason why it was MFI'd, P3008 is now admitted into evidence. If there's any reason to revisit the translation, we'll hear from the Defence. Further, I would like to invite the Defence to prepare for making submissions on the bar table motion in relation to Witness Treanor. Eighteen documents have been bar tabled. The Chamber would like to hear on shortest notice from the Defence in relation to those 18 documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Stojanovic and I met with Ms. Bibles the other day, and as I had communicated yesterday, I believe the -- there had been 20 and we said we did not have an objection to 18, so I'm assuming that the 18 are those that we did not have an objection to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that's the case. I see that Ms. Stewart is nodding. So you left out the two contested ones. Under those circumstances, Madam Registrar is invited to prepare to assign numbers to the 18 documents. Once she has done so, we'll decide on admission. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would like to now turn your attention to 12 May 1992. Have you reviewed Ratko Mladic's speech to the 16th Assembly of the Serbian People of BiH on this date?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Your Honours. And that can be found on English page 40 of Part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In reviewing this speech, what general observations did you have or do have you about General Mladic's references to his experiences in Croatia as an officer in the JNA 9th Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, General Mladic mentions his experiences in Croatia as the deputy commander and Chief of Staff of the 9th Corps, and subsequently as the commander of the 9 Corps headquarters located in Knin, in order to illustrate his interpretation and his understanding of strategic goals focusing, in particular, on the first and the sixth -- excuse me, and the fifth goal. So the first one, the separation of the people, and the fifth the maintaining the division of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please bring up Exhibit P431. The Prosecution would like page 42, the bottom half in English, and page 35 of the B/C/S. Mr. Theunens before -- we're going to go through portions of this speech in greater detail. Before doing so, I would like to simply ask you whether you found references in General Mladic's speech to events which are part of your analysis in Part 1, section 3, of your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honours. And the most obvious ones are General Mladic addressing Mr. Milan Martic, who is in the audience of the 16th Assembly Session when highlighting the need for single and unified command and control over the forces and refer -- he does that by referring to the situation in Kijevo where he established single command and control over SAO Krajina also known as Martic police and forces of the 9th corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if I can interrupt you just so we go through this step by step in this speech. I believe in the English version, it's towards the bottom half on the screen starting in the middle. I'd like to direct your attention to the portion that states: "The Knin Corps was successful because under a single command in the zone of the corps were the JNA, the Territorial Defence forces, and Martic's police, isn't that right, Martic? And because he and I, I call him and say, give me 40 policemen here at Kijevo and you took part in the fighting, isn't that right Milan? And we did what we planned. And we planned. And we will have artillery here and this artillery acts." In the context of the materials reviewed, could you please tell us what General Mladic is talking about in this specific passage.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, General Mladic is talking about the operations led by the JNA to take control over Kijevo, and this took place if I'm not mistaken in August 1991, Kijevo being located on the main supply road between municipalities or locations that were already under Serbian/JNA control in southern Dalmatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was the objective of the attack on Kijevo in August 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the objective was to remove the Croatian police station which was seen as a symbol of Croatian control over this -- yeah, Croatian town, in order to achieve territorial integrity between other -- or with other surrounding municipalities and terrain that was already under, as I said, Serb/JNA control.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Throughout this speech, General Mladic makes a total of six references to Martic. Again, based on your review of materials, could you describe the nature of Mladic and Martic's relationship prior to 12 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say at face value already the excerpt of the speech, the quite personal way General Mladic addresses Martic shows that their relations went beyond purely professional co-operation, and I would say that there is even mutual sympathy or at least mutual agreement about the goals they are pursuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After May 1992, were there any VRS operations in Bosnia that included Serb forces provided by Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honours. We have -- I mean, two examples. First of all, there are the so-called corridor operations which are conducted in June and November 1992. And, secondly, there is -- there are the operations in the so-called Sadinska [phoen] Krajina in the latter half of 1994 and running into 1995 which, I mean, are best known through the separate command -- the so-called Pauk Command that was established, and these operations were intended to support Fikret Abdic against the ABiH 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 35 of the English, the bottom half, and page 29 of the B/C/S. Mr. Theunens, I'm going to be directing your attention to the part of General Mladic's speech where he states: "There's nowhere they can go. One of the reasons is because the head of the Dragan of fundamentalism lies beneath our hammer. To tell the truth, what I have seen - and must tell you that I've seen very bad picture - and I've ordered officers from the Knin Corps to come who will very soon change this picture. One cannot take Sarajevo by spitting at it from a mortar or a howitzer." Were there any officers brought over from the Knin Corps and incorporated as officers of the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know of at least of General Tolimir who became the assistant commander for security and intelligence in the VRS Main Staff. At this moment, I'm not sure whether General Manojlo Milovanovic, who was the Chief of Staff -- or who became the Chief of Staff of the VRS Main Staff also served with General Mladic in the 9th Corps. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 38, the bottom half, in English, and page 31 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Coming off this past reference to Sarajevo, I'd also now like to consider a couple additional portions. I -- I'd like to discuss the sections independently and then I will ask you to provide more general comments. The first section is: "The army must have unified command. And when we start fighting over Sarajevo, we must not say before the international public or tell Mr. Ostojic to pass it to them, we are going to shut down your water and power supply, why should I explain to him what I'm going to do? He will see what I am going to do. And we have to put a ring around the dragon's head of Sarajevo this very moment, and only those whom we let out should be allowed out," and it continues. What do you make of these statements by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in relation to -- to Sarajevo, as we know, the 5th Corps does not consist of taking control of the whole of Sarajevo but consists of maintaining the division of Sarajevo because of the symbolic and -- importance of Sarajevo, and General Mladic explains then to the assembly members how this can be best achieved --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could just pause there. Continuing on a few lines down, General Mladic states: "What is it, we do not know, damage, we should fix it, no, we will fix it slowly. And the same with the electrical power. Zadar and Sibenik and Split, they disconnected the army's power supply, and the army had none for six months."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. ... is there any reason why the speed of speech is not the -- the volume of the speech is not such that it's inaudible because I've warned now again and again, and I do not intend to continue doing that. Consultation will only be allowed if it's inaudible for the remainder of the courtroom. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm told it's again a problem with the monitor, that the B/C/S is not legible on the monitor. And I don't know whether it's the size of the text, or yesterday we had a problem where half of the B/C/S was truncated because of the settings of the monitor, which I did fix by the end of the day. But that is what I'm told is the issue that was just raised by Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the B/C/S is the only text on the monitor, and I take it that is the case for Mr. Mladic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Actually, the B/C/S and the English are on the monitor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both are on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we should zoom in in such a way that it becomes legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see it's in Cyrillic. I don't know if Mr. Ivetic can assist us maybe with locating the passage that I was referring to. And I believe it was towards the bottom of the Cyrillic, but it may be onto the next page. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, any way you could assist?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it may be on the next page of the Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's the very last line of this page and will go onto the next page, so the text is actually not on the screen. That's the remainder of the text. The reference to Mr. Ostojic is in the middle of the last line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we now looking at the page where it started or are we looking at the next page? The next page. Okay. Yes. It may not be easy to read it, just as it is not easy in English. If Mr. Mladic has found it, and if he's able to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, otherwise -- otherwise we'd have to -- yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I -- I was -- we were trying to get a hard copy organised for the general that might assist. I'm told the text is still too small to read on the monitor. But as far as I know, there is no way to show only the B/C/S to the general and then have everyone else follow the English. So I think that technologically speaking, we are stuck with what we have in the monitors with a double screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that one of the solutions might be that all those who have an opportunity to move to the other screen and read there in English, that we would have a larger presentation of the B/C/S text for the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will also try to read the full passage slowly in cases the accused would like to follow it on the B/C/S channel as I'm reading it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, every effort being made to -- could you please start in slowly reading the passage that you would like to draw the attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the passage we were discussing -- I'd like to discuss with you, says: "What is it, we do not know, damage, we should fix it, no, we will fix it, slowly. And the same with the electrical power. Zadar and Sibenik and Split, they disconnected the army's power supply, the army had none for six months, but I told them, while I am here, you will not get it. And they didn't, apart from when I felt like letting them have some." The sentence continues but I'm going to just stop there. End quote. Could you please explain General Mladic's reference -- references to past events in Zadar, Sibenik, and Split in the context of his previous statements about Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, General Mladic explains to the -- to the assembly members how he had used the control of public services, like water and electricity provision, in the conflict with the Croats; i.e., when the Croats are to block JNA garrisons and barracks and installations in the cities mentioned in the transcript, he retaliated by cutting off water and electricity to these cities. And he uses this experience to illustrate to the assembly members how the 5th goal -- or the 5th strategic goal should be implemented, i.e., maintain the division of Sarajevo. So by using Serbian control over water, gas, and electricity distribution to the city as a, quote/unquote, I mean, in my language, quote/unquote weapon in order to put pressure on the enemy. And I refer to an order in -- during the conflict on page 257 of my report, an order by General Manojlo Milovanovic, that confirms this interpretation of Mr. Mladic's words during the assembly session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Continuing on and in the next sentence on the screen before you, General Mladic states: "Therefore, we have to wisely tell the world it was they who were shooting, hit the transmission line, and the power went off. They were shooting at the water supply facilities. There was a power cut at such and such a place, we are doing our best to repair this [sic], this is what diplomacy is." How do these last statements by General Mladic relate to events that happened in Sarajevo after May 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I think I'm going to object because I just checked the Rule 65 ter summary for this witness and he's being presented as an expert on command and control and now I think he is becoming a historical expert witness which is not noticed on the Rule 65 ter summary for this witness, nor in the Rule 94 bis submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you explain exactly what you meant by historical witness or is it context of the in the way in which command and control is exercised?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it says here: [As read] "He will testify to the composition and command structure of the Bosnian Serb TO, the establishment and functioning of the Army of Republika Srpska, and its co-ordination and co-operation with other Serb military and police forces from other parts of the former Yugoslavia; in particular, he will address the status and military activities of volunteers, and volunteer units, and forces of or associated otherwise by the MUP Serbia, including their relationship to and subordination within the other military forces on the ground such as the Army of Republika Srpska, the JNA, VJ, and local Serb TO and special police units." What we've had from the last --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What we've had with the last several questions has been this witness attempting to give a historical context to an interpretation of documents not related to any command and control questions but rather trying to give the Prosecution's arguments as to documents and to give a historical opinion about things. We've had several witnesses who have done that, Professor Donia and I believe Professor Treanor for one, but they were noticed as having been able to do that. This witness was presented as a military expert, and I think we're going outwith what has been presented as his purported expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I see on the screen the quote that I just read has been cut off at the top. But my question was: How do these last statements, if you still recall them, by General Mladic relate to events that subsequently happened in Sarajevo after May 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I illustrate in the report, when I discuss the authority of General Mladic as commander of the Main Staff, I conclude based on the documents I reviewed that control over humanitarian aid, including public facilities like gas, water, and electricity distribution, in those areas where Serbs could -- could exercise control over these facilities, are important tools or weapons for the Bosnian Serbs to achieve the Bosnian Serb strategic goals. And General Mladic explains here to the assembly members how this should be done, and he even makes a reference to how this can play a role in -- in negotiations, in my view, by referring to the concept of diplomacy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 732. Mr. Theunens, before you will be appearing a -- or the 1991 JNA 9th Corps combat readiness report from General Mladic dated 22 January 1992. Just quickly. At this time, was the JNA 9th Corps part of the 2nd Military District?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was Your Honours. The 2nd Military District being established early January 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On the first page of this report, General Mladic refers to the elimination of the weakness in the concept of All People's Defence or ONO or self-protection system or DSZ. What is he talking about?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, General Mladic is talking about issues related to weakness in command and control, i.e., that initially when the Bosnian Serbs established their own armed structures in this case in Croatia, local Serb TO, local Serb MUP, or Martic police, these units are not necessarily subordinated to the JNA. We also see the appearance of volunteers/paramilitary formations where the same problems occur, and then from also earlier orders from General Mladic as well as actually the commander of 9 Corps prior to him, General Vukovic, clear instructions are given to subordinate all what I call Serb forces to the JNA in a given zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 5 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S. I would note that the information we're about to discuss continues onto page 4 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the bottom paragraph on this page, under section 4 on the basic experience drawn from the use of units. In the paragraph, General Mladic discusses the carrying out of the first stage of operation with the engagement of tactical and combat groups --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With the engagement of tactical and combat groups throughout the 9th Corps area of responsibility. In reviewing this report, can you tell us, as commander of the VRS, did General Mladic draw upon these earlier experiences to facilitate his exercise of single authority over tactical and operational groups?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and I would even widen the issue. It's not just these operational groups or tactical groups, but it's just he takes active steps from the very beginning that he is appointed commander of the Main Staff to enforce a single and unified command and control in the areas where the VRS is operating. And we see successive orders to achieve that. And, I mean, if you want, I can give examples but otherwise they're in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could please move to the bottom of page 6 in the English and page 4 which I believe is currently on the screen in the B/C/S. At the bottom of this page, General Mladic mentions the positive effect of "the successful placing of the SAO Krajina TO under the single command of the 9th Corps on the ability of the 9th Corps to conduct combat operations in a wide area."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have page 6 on our screens? I don't think we have. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you re-start, Mr. Weber, or at least draw our attention to the portion you just read. I think it's the bottom part.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then... yes. We've --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- had an opportunity to read it. Please proceed, where you stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Theunens, would be could you please explain how the placing of the TO under a single command would facilitate an army's ability to conduct operations in a wider area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I mean, single command I would say in any circumstance is the easy situation. If you have -- it's the easiest, sorry, situation. If -- in a military context you have two commanders, you can have chaos because a subordinate should only have one commander. Even if we're talking about two different units here - on the one hand, JNA; on the other hand, Krajina Serb TO - by that time they are pursuing the same goals or at least coherent goals. Most effective way to achieve that, i.e., to have a unified system of command and control is, as I mentioned, to have only one commander which, in practical terms, means to subordinate the TO, the Bosnian -- excuse me, the SAO Krajina TO to the JNA 9th Corps by attaching these SAO Krajina TO units to units of the JNA 9 Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After General Mladic was appointed commander of the VRS, did his incorporation of the existing SRBiH TO units into the VRS structure increase or not the ability of the VRS in a similar way?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. And I refer to the June -- the 4th of June, 1992, order by General Mladic which is footnote 260. Then there is the September 1992 report by General Mladic, footnote 262, and both in Part 2 of the report, and of course there is the 1993 analysis of combat readiness report which clearly highlight the benefits of subordinating all units to the single command of the VRS in order to achieve the said goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to the top and middle of the page. In these paragraphs, there's reference to successful tasks being carried out related to the lifting of the blockade on a number of places, including Zadar, Sibenik, and Split. Mr. Mladic -- General Mladic also indicates that these offensive combat operations forced the enemy to negotiate, and he then describes how artillery would soften targets, direct fire artillery groups would destroy the observed targets - God bless you, Ms. Stewart - and infantry protected with tanks and armoured combat vehicles would take control of features. Do the tactics applied in these locations as described by General Mladic bear any similarity to how General Mladic pursued strategic goal number 5?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say to a certain extent, Your Honours, because Sarajevo did not see so much the use of VRS infantry for obvious reasons because, first of all, achieving goals in a buildup area where infantry is -- I mean, on the one hand it is more effective than using tanks, but it requires a lot of manpower and it also requires -- no, it will also involve high losses. One of the deficiencies the VRS was facing throughout the conflict was a lack of manpower, compared to the ABiH. So for Sarajevo, for the fifth goal, I would say that the emphasis lay on the use of artillery and other indirect fire weapons that were deployed on the hills and mountains surrounding Sarajevo in addition to what we discussed earlier, i.e., the control over public facilities; namely water, gas, and electricity provision.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 16 of the English and page 9 of the B/C/S of this report. In this section of the report, General Mladic discusses the preparation and mobilisation of RJ of the 9th Corps in several stages. He describes a partial mobilisation between 21 and 29 June 1991. If you could assist us, did this occur right around the time that General Mladic was transferred to the JNA 9th Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, I believe he was transferred -- I mean, he took over as Chief of Staff and deputy commander of the 9th Corps, if I remember well, on 20th of -- of June -- sorry, 30th of July of 1991. And prior to that, he was the chief of the Department for Operations and Training in the 9th -- in the 9th Corps. So yes, indeed, it coincides.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 121 of Part 1, you list General Mladic's positions including his initial assignment as the chief of the operations, which you just mentioned, between June and July 1991. In this position, what were the responsibilities of then-Colonel Mladic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the Department for Operations and Training is, as the name says it, is responsible for training. And again based -- this is based on the instructions from the commander which training programmes have to be conducted. This concerns both individual training as well as collective training or at unit level. He is also responsible for drawing the operational orders. You could compare it with what is in western militaries called the J or the G3, so the -- the person responsible for operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Returning to the report before us, it states that then from 19 to 24 September 1991, all corps units were fully mobilised. And in the next paragraph it states that: "From 20 September to 30 November 1991, subordinated units constantly grew." We see here then a reference to newly established TO units being incorporated into the 9th Corps and soldiers being recruited from the corps area of responsibility and other republics. Did these events occur after General Mladic was appointed deputy commander of the JNA 9th Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During and after, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Between 20 September and 30 November 1991, did the JNA 9th Corps take over areas of the Croatian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would raise an objection as to the relevance of 30 November 1991 which is outside the temporal scope of the indictment and the Croatian Krajina which is outside the geographic scope of the indictment. This is an issue we have raised ever since the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution, and I think we at this point in time need to have an order from the Chamber so we know what is part of this case and what is not part of this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, the Defence statement is inaccurate in terms of the temporal scope. We alleged in the indictment that it began in October 1991. With respect to the relevance of this material, we've stated it clearly multiple times in submissions. Your Honours, the conduct of General Mladic is relevant to this case, and the Defence has even tried to rely on the fact that he was off in Croatia as mitigating his responsibility for events that occurred once he became commander of the VRS. As Mr. Theunens has testified, there was a pattern between what General Mladic's conduct was when he was commander of the JNA -- well, when he was assigned to the JNA 9th Corps and when he immediately became commander of the VRS. Mr. Theunens has also testified to a number of facts already that show that General Mladic immediately implemented things that he specifically learned as part of the JNA 9th Corps immediately when he became commander of the VRS. So in terms of substantive relevance, I believe that the threshold has been met. I would just ask: Your Honours specifically instructed the Prosecution as part of its examination to lead evidence from Part 1 of its report and, of course, I am applying your guidance in doing that right now, trying, of course, to go to the pertinent documents from General Mladic himself, and on top of it, Your Honours, you've acknowledged in multiple ways that events in Croatia to some extent, as it relates to the accused, are relevant to these proceedings. And just to name the two most prominent examples: The Chamber has admitted General Mladic's personal notebooks from this time throughout -- updating all the way back to June 1991, and also Mladic audio recordings recovered from seizures of premises associated exhibited with the accused containing General Mladic's statements at this time. Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, any response. Specifically on the temporal scope of the indictment and the Defence relying on what happened in -- during the time Mr. Mladic was in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Be happy to, Your Honour. This witness is an expert witness supposedly on the command and control of the VRS which was established in May of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I could --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Therefore the witness is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I could interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue was first temporal scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are now addressing how this witness is presented. Now, relevance of the evidence and whether something falls within the scope of the expertise of a witness are two different matters. Would you please specifically first address the temporal scope where Mr. Weber said --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm attempting to, Your Honour. May 1992 is within the indictment when it is alleged that General Mladic became part of the -- of the plan by becoming part of the alleged JCE by becoming part of the VRS Main Staff; therefore, events of 1991 are outwith the temporal scope of the allegations in the indictment. Furthermore, this witness's testimony was said to be related to the command and control of the VRS in the early days of its formation, which is again May 1992. Therefore, we have multiple problems with allowing this witness now to opine as to matters that go to 1991 and which go to Croatia which do not, in fact, arise out of his opining about the command and control of the VRS in May of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic, I haven't heard you yet on the Defence relying at various occasions on events in 1991 in Croatia. Or at least considering of such -- relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the Defence objecting to evidence is to be interpreted as "relying," we have objected continuously to inclusion of events from 1991 by saying he was not part of the VRS. We have said that since day one. We had in our pre-trial brief. It was part of the pre-trial conference. That's why I'm asking Your Honours to finally rule on the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could you address the two issues I specifically have drawn the attention of Mr. Ivetic to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- with respect to the Defence relying on Mr. Mladic's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps I first -- Mr. Ivetic, paragraph 5 on the joint criminal enterprise says that Ratko Mladic was, as of the 12th of May, 1992, a key member of an overarching joint criminal enterprise which lasted from at least October 1991 until 30th of November 1995. Do you say that every moment before Mr. Mladic became a key member, and it's not said he became a -- no, became a key member, that everything that happened in the joint criminal enterprise which is described as at least from October 1991 would be irrelevant for this case? Is that the position of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we're saying that the indictment with the paragraph that you've just read for General Mladic relates the start date to the 12th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you say if you joins a joint criminal enterprise in May 1992, then that joint criminal enterprise, which is described of having existed before, is irrelevant for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I'm saying that in terms of the notice requirements of the jurisprudence and the pleading requirements of an indictment, when one pleads that the participation of an accused begins on a certain date, the Trial Chamber is presumably going to be focused on the activities of the accused that date and thereafter. Otherwise, the Defence is not in a position to know what case it must respond to and what evidence it must bring to rebut the Prosecution's case, as was raised in the Defence pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber denies the objection. Based on the temporal scope, what has been dealt with is to some extent within the time scope described in the indictment, although giving history and given context and the Chamber accepts the relevance of this context. Then we have the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the geographic scope ... for the geographic scope, it similarly gives context, not only in terms of geography but also in terms of the history of the accused which may give additional context on what happened at the later stages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, then I renew my objection this witness giving historical expert testimony for which has not been notified under 65 ter or Rule 94 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was denied already and that is still denied. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens my last question was between 20 September and 30 November 1991, did the JNA 9th Corps participate in take-overs of areas of the Croatian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Returning to the document before us, General Mladic then discusses new motorised and a new infantry brigade joining the 9th Corps, and the implementation of replenishment plan in four municipalities within the self-declared Serb Autonomous Region of the Croatian Krajina. General Mladic then goes on to state: "The Serbs made up 97 per cent of the corps units and members of other ethnic groups made up 3 per cent. This ratio did not correspond to the ethnic composition of the population in the area of responsibility of the corps." Is the ethnic composition of the JNA 9th Corps, described by General Mladic at this time, consistent with the transformation of the JNA that occurred throughout the former Yugoslavia which you discuss in Part 1 of your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and I mean, if you want I can explain it because it's a bit of a complex issue. It's not just a matter of people being removed or -- or people not just -- not wanting to join the JNA anymore when they are mobilised. I mean, there is a whole evolution occurring, and the end state is that, okay, the JNA in Croatia -- or what remains of JNA is -- is pursuing mainly Serbian goals, and I mean by that that the JNA is enforcing control or Serbian control over territories that are considered Serb in close co-operation; i.e., supervising in a military sense, local Serb TO, forces consisting of TO, and MUP local Serb forces, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just so we have it on the record, I would like you to confirm what -- the opinion that that's stated on page 132 of Part 1. You conclude based on the instructions of the SFRY Presidency and Veljko Kadijevic's orders that: "The JNA ceased to be the SFRY army and instead, at least in Croatia, gradually develops into a mainly Serb force, serving Serbian goals. The JNA's role has been transformed from one of interposing among the conflicting parties to one of creation and control of Serb-held areas in those parts of Croatia that the Serbian leadership considered Serb." Is that your opinion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my conclusion, Your Honours, on the basis of the material I have reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does this report that we've been looking at from General Mladic support this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, Your Honours. It's one of the many documents I reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 131 of Part 1, you refer to General Mladic's 30 December 1991 closing speech at the meeting of the 9th Corps combat readiness, and you conclude that this speech -- that in this speech Mladic demonstrated the coherence between the operations of the 9th Corps with the earlier instructions of Kadijevic and Adzic on the SFRY armed forces goals of the war in Croatia. Could you please confirm that this is your conclusion for the record?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is Your Honours. And if you want -- again, I can explain it both on -- on the -- the goals as such but also the terminology that is being used to describe the conflict in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 732 into evidence, which we've been discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We would object in so far as it is not relevant to the time-period of the indictment on the geographic scope of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. It is sufficiently related to the charges in the indictment, it gives context, and may be relevant for drawing parallels.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 00732 receives number P3051.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3051 is admitted into evidence. Time for a break, Mr. Weber. Could Mr. Theunens be escorted out of the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the opportunity to be clearer in my instructions as far as P3008 is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I had not specifically instructed or granted leave to the Registrar to replace the English translation of P3008 by the newly uploaded one. That was the new translation where "supervision" was changed into "control." We take a break, and we'll resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll briefly deal with a few procedural matters. The first is the -- is a decision on the admission of the Treanor reports. The Prosecution has now uploaded the redacted version of the Treanor reports under 65 ter numbers 02881a and 11849a. The Chamber admits these redacted the versions of the reports into evidence, and Madam Registrar you are hereby instructed to replace the documents under Exhibit numbers P3003 and P3004 with the newly uploaded reports. Perhaps, meanwhile, the witness can be escorted into the courtroom. And I continue with Treanor bar table documents. The Chamber has received a list of 18 bar table documents that the Prosecution wishes to tender with Expert Witness Treanor. The Defence indicated in court that it did not oppose the admission of those 18. Madam Registrar has reserved exhibit numbers P3033 through 3050 for these documents. The Chamber hereby admits the documents into evidence under these numbers. We'll wait for the witness to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it helps expedite things, I will now be immediately calling up Exhibit P1959.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And where before the break I addressed that I had not previously granted leave to replace the English translation of P3008, I still didn't do it. It's hereby done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seats, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1959.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
